# Marin standup — Week ending Fri, Nov 13, 2026

**Previous standup**: [Week of November 2, 2026 standup](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11169)

## Amy Sartran ([@asartran](https://github.com/asartran))

### What you did this week

- Got the Snowball training loop ready, 2 nodes of MI355x. Checkpointing, restarts and real data all work. Built the Snowball-mix ladder datasets on GCS, and drafted an outline for a decontaminated Harrier training set for the full snowball run.
- Mostly reviewing and benchmarking Marco’s AMD PR stack(#11122-#11126, #11140-#11148, #11150-#11159). We’re reworking to avoid touching too much of the model config and having AMD-specific implementation logic outside the training code.
- Some CI fixes. One makes pre-commit catch stale vendored lockfiles, which failed 87 CI jobs last week ([#11423](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11423)). The other fixes one of the two failures that have broken the nightly slow job since Nov 3 [#11425](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11425), [#11427](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11427).

### What you plan to do next week

- Finish writing the Snowball run plan and send AMD the dataset and storage sizes.
- Review Marco’s restructured PRs and Pratik’s checkpointing fix (supercedes our [#10969](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10969)).
- Build the Harrier ladder caches once the decontamination question is settled.

sourceStates.title: [levanter] Weight eval bits per byte by bytes
sourceStates.body:
Compute `eval/bpb`, each set's `bpb` and the group keys such as `eval/paloma/bpb` as the scored text's total loss over its total bytes, instead of a token-weighted mean of per-batch bits per byte. The evaluator keeps a running mean of bytes per scored token beside its running mean loss and divides the two. `LabeledEvaluator` weights its per-label bits per byte by bytes, which gives the same value unless a batch holds only zero-byte targets.

With token weights the logged value depends on how eval batches split the data, and the group keys weighted each set by `bpb_per_tag.total`, which held token counts. In the new test, two sets with one-byte and two-byte tokens and one nat of loss per token, main logs 1.082 bits per byte (the token-weighted mean of 1.443 and 0.721) instead of 0.962 (2 nats over 3 bytes). #10968 measured +3.6% to +4.7% on `paloma/dolma_100_programing_languages` along the `lc1-h235` ladder and traced #9126's code BPB regression to this weighting.

The loss on a zero-byte target such as EOS counts toward the total whichever batch it lands in. A set whose scored targets have no bytes logs no bits per byte and stays out of the macros, and a group or eval with no scored bytes logs no micro bits per byte. Logged values change for runs with a tokenizer; per-set loss does not. The other open defects of #10968 (partial UTF-8 tokens, scored text versus source text, MoE auxiliary loss) are separate.

Part of #10968

sourceStates.title: [eval] Evaluate Hero at multiple context lengths
sourceStates.body:
Hero evals score 4K and the current training length, adding fixed 65K and 262K evals only once training reaches those lengths. Each distinct length has its own metrics, such as `eval_dropless/seq_len_4096/paloma/macro_loss`; `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` continues to report the training-length eval.

All eval lengths keep the training context-parallel width. The dropless mesh and PartitionSpec renaming reuse #10709's implementation: each device retains its training context group and uses its training (data, expert) group for eval data. Eval therefore reuses the device groups whose replacement caused NCCL memory growth in #10709. Batch sizes stay within the configured global padded-token budget per evaluation batch, rounded down to whole batch shards.

Continuous-text validation retains incomplete final sequences with right padding and excludes padding from attention and loss, including the real-to-pad prediction. Short Paloma corpora remain in the long-context aggregate. Validation sequence statistics include the final partial sequence; stored token counts exclude padding. Overall loss and bits-per-byte macros exclude tags with no scored tokens.

CPU tests check device groups, per-device parameter shards and the multi-length eval-to-training handoff. No GPU rehearsal of this revision has run.

Part of #8435.

sourceStates.title: [levanter] Normalize policy logits on fixed FP32 row tiles
sourceStates.body:
Add a shared FP32 log-normalizer and log-softmax for vocabulary logits. A
fixed row tile gives each token the same reduction schedule when scored
alone or in a learner batch. This prevents a change in batch shape alone
from changing policy log probabilities on TPU.

The primitive preserves leading-axis sharding and gathers vocabulary shards
before reduction. The fused cross-entropy reference shares the accurate
reduction. Serving and learner callers can adopt the fixed tiling separately.

sourceStates.title: [rl] Retain partial generations at canonical turn deadlines
sourceStates.body:
Canonical task evaluations can discard an active non-streaming decode when the turn deadline fires before vLLM returns a complete model turn. In the reported Micro210 evaluation, 78 of 434 single-turn reasoning trials were archived as zero-token unavailable rows. The archive does not show whether the engine generated tokens.

Carry request-correlated engine scheduling notices through the cancellable Ray response stream. Execution budgets arm at the first request and rebase when the engine schedules it; a transport without scheduling notices retains the old turn deadline. A separate cumulative 2,280-second allowance per attempt bounds admission wait. Before the nearest remaining execution deadline, request vLLM's native partial abort and await the original collector. The returned sampled tokens, logprobs, routes, and policy-step stamps reach the real verifier. Requests with no sampled tokens remain unavailable. Canonical evaluation uses this shared path without a recipe cutoff. The current Pi relay carries the trial clock and a bounded HTTP watchdog across its callback task.

The transport marks a deadline-triggered partial abort without choosing a rollout stop reason. The recorder attributes the partial to the nearest model-turn, total-turn, or attempt budget, then stops the trial after grading. Rollouts report queue wait separately from generation time. Engine timing records include engine and request IDs for slow-decode attribution. The CPU regressions cover active partial returns, saturated admission, never-scheduled requests, raw and chat transport, deadline attribution, and relay timeouts. GPU boundary behavior remains unverified; the new code affects future jobs only. This ports the relevant behavior from draft #11120, with adaptations for current `main`.

The task-local `ContextVar` carries the trial clock into detached callbacks explicitly. The abort RPC's boolean only reports whether an active sampled request was aborted; the caller always awaits the original collector. Deadline attribution stays in the recorder's existing cancellation and turn-recording sequence.

Pi and mini-swe episode harness revisions advance because the shared relay changes their behavior. The generated SkyRL author schema includes the admission allowance.

Validation: Marin lint and type checks passed; 277 RolloutEngine, 11 Shellbox, 55 SkyRL transport/task, four harness-revision, and two schema-generation tests passed. The broad root test runner stopped before collection because its environment lacked `pytest-xdist`; package-level tests used their configured environments. All required CI checks passed after retrying the Levanter serialization shard; two prior attempts failed in untouched TensorStore tests.

Part of #12360.

sourceStates.title: [evals] Run SWE-bench Multilingual's agent offline and grade it in a separate verifier
sourceStates.body:
SWE-bench Multilingual's agents had internet access, and some read the upstream fix from GitHub before passing. This runs the agent offline and grades it in Harbor's separate verifier: a fresh machine from the task's image, with the network its tests need to install their log parser, which applies a patch of the agent's workspace.

The changes are package edits in the dataset's definition, so the published packages are untouched:

| Edit | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `allow_internet = false` for the agent | No upstream fixes |
| `[verifier.environment]` with the network, built from a copy of `environment/Dockerfile` | A fresh grading machine from the same image |
| A collect step that diffs the workspace against a git tree recorded when the image is built | The agent's changes, including edits to files the image leaves untracked |
| `test.sh` applies the patch first | Grading as before, against the agent's changes |

New files over 1 MiB stay out of the patch, and a patch that fails to apply records an infrastructure error. Terminus 2's images install `tmux` at build time, since it would otherwise install it at startup. `PackageCopy` is a new package edit for adding the verifier's Dockerfile. The version bump starts fresh corpora.

Validation and the leak this closes are in the issue. Depends on #12365.

sourceStates.title: [evals] Launch eval policy candidates with policy launch
sourceStates.body:
Add `policy launch`, which submits one candidate's evaluations under an eval policy through the existing launcher. It resolves the candidate, applies each evaluation's output limit and seed to its catalog selection, groups the evaluations onto servers, and submits one job per server, labelled with the policy version, without waiting.

```
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.policy.cli launch --policy marin-2026-11-20-trial \
  --candidate qwen3.6-35b-a3b --priority interactive [--evaluations a,b] [--limit 20] [--federated-cluster C] [--dry-run]
```

Each candidate runs on one server at its serving window (#12298). The server runs `EVALUATIONS_PER_SERVER` (4) evaluations at once instead of one at a time; requests within each evaluation were already concurrent. Every server runs the candidate's serving config with its checkpoint-derived settings resolved, so a run's identity doesn't depend on which evaluations share its server. A candidate is split across servers only when its evaluations' judges need different keys, since a launch hands its judges one key. For the trial policy that is one server per candidate. A checkpoint that serves less than its catalog window is rejected before submission. Running evaluations in parallel gives up per-evaluation inference metrics: the runner captures server metrics only when one evaluation has the server to itself.

`--dry-run` prints each server's accelerator, cluster and window, and each evaluation's limit, output cap, seed, agent budgets and results path. A full run (no `--limit`) refuses a checkout with uncommitted changes, or a recorded commit other than HEAD (the launcher prefers `MARIN_GIT_SHA` or `GIT_COMMIT` when set), so its records name the commit that ran; a smoke run proceeds with a warning.

`LaunchSpec` gains `default_seed`. The launcher used to give curated runs without a seed a seed of 0 on servers that accept seeds; a policy launch passes `None`, so an evaluation the policy leaves unseeded takes its protocol's trial seeds, as the policy schema documents. Other launches keep 0.

Records need no new fields: they carry the policy version, the commit, and the resolved model, corpus, agent and run settings, which `policy status` and `policy verify` (a later PR) compare against the policy as resolved in the current checkout.

A dry run of GSM8K 0-shot, FinanceBench, MRCR-32k, AIME24 and SWE-bench Verified for Qwen3.6 resolves to one 4×H100 server at 73,728 tokens. A 20-item smoke run of that set succeeded under the earlier two-server grouping, and `policy verify` (#12216) finds all five runs valid: AIME24 0.970, FinanceBench 0.500, GSM8K 0.750, MRCR-32k 0.905, SWE-bench Verified 0.550.

sourceStates.title: [evals] Add policy status and verify, and pin released policies to a tag
sourceStates.body:
This PR adds two commands for following a policy's runs once they're launched:

- `policy status` shows, for each evaluation of a candidate, whether its full and smoke runs exist and are valid, so you can see what's done and what still needs launching.
- `policy verify RUN_ID...` checks any run against the policy and lists what differs.

```
evaluation     full run  smoke run (limit 5)
financebench   not run   valid accuracy=1.000 5/50 @a7a2dfd
gpqa-diamond   not run   valid accuracy=0.800 15/594 @a7a2dfd
ds-1000-local  not run   valid reward=0.200 5/200 @a7a2dfd
```

(`status` output from the end-to-end check below: Qwen3.5-9B under a three-evaluation copy of the trial policy.)

So that `status` can find runs, policy launches now derive their run IDs from the policy version, each run's inputs, the server's vLLM build and accelerator, and, for an agent, how many attempts run at once (the smaller of the evaluation's and the model's bounds). The same launch always writes to the same paths. `status` reads one record per evaluation instead of searching, and re-running a launch skips runs that succeeded and reruns ones that failed.

Both commands compare a record with what the current checkout would launch:

| Check | Catches |
| --- | --- |
| Model | another revision, tokenizer, serving config or window |
| Evaluation | another corpus, protocol, output cap, seed, judge, agent limits or item limit |
| Evaluator runtime | a changed TaskSpec driver behind unchanged settings |
| Window | a server that reported another window than the policy's |
| Run ID | another vLLM build, accelerator or agent concurrency, which no recorded field shows |
| Outcome | a failed run, or a full run whose selection left items undecided; items its protocol excludes, such as MRCR conversations too long for its window, don't count as missing |

A run can match the policy and still be broken, for example a server that produces noise until every reply hits its output cap. Both commands mark such a run with ⚠ and say why, without changing its state: more than 10% of single-turn replies stopped at their output cap, or fewer than 95% of a task's attempts were scored. `verify` exits non-zero unless every run is valid.

Differences are named by field, for example `eval.curated.settings.seed: ran 0, policy gives null`. The comparison uses the launcher's own identity functions, so "same run" has one definition. A run whose inputs differ and that came from an older commit is reported as `differs from this checkout` rather than `invalid`, because any later change to a model config or corpus changes a run's inputs.

Tested on records written by the runner's own record writer: valid runs, failed runs, a wrong window, a full run missing items, inputs that differ from the same or another commit, and runs either side of each warning threshold.

End to end, I launched Qwen3.5-9B through `policy launch` under a three-evaluation copy of the trial policy (GPQA, FinanceBench with its Together judge, and DS-1000 on Daytona), at 5 items:

- A launch whose inference broker was preempted wrote `infra_failed` records. `status` reported both as invalid with the error, and relaunching reran them at the same paths.
- On TPU, vLLM served Qwen3.5 without a working linear-attention kernel and every reply was noise. Those runs were policy-conformant, which is why the ⚠ warnings were added: 10 of 15 GPQA replies hit their cap.
- On one H100 all three runs were valid, with the scores shown above. Relaunching the same command from a later commit wrote to the same paths, skipped every evaluation, and started no model server.

`verify` on the trial policy's 20-item Qwen3.6 smoke runs, served on 4×H100, found all five valid: AIME24 0.970, FinanceBench 0.500, GSM8K 0.750, MRCR 32k 0.905 and SWE-bench Verified 0.550.

I also ran `verify` on two existing GPQA smoke runs launched outside the policy. It read their archives and flagged the missing policy version, ad-hoc model names, a different corpus and seed 0.

A policy version names its evaluations but not the code that runs them, so two runs of one version could come from different commits. A policy marked `released` therefore launches only from a clean checkout of its tag, `eval-policy-<version>`, and `status` and `verify` check it only from a clean checkout of that tag and mark its runs from any other commit invalid. Its run IDs include the tag's commit, so runs made before the release, under the same version, never stand in for the release's, and relaunching from the tag still resumes failed runs. A release is cut by setting `released=True` in its policy module, merging, then tagging the merged commit; a fix to a released policy is a new version.

Not included: jobs that are still queued or running, which have no record until they end; EvalDash admission.

sourceStates.title: [evals] Launch policy evaluations for several candidates or a checkpoint
sourceStates.body:
`policy launch` runs one declared candidate per command. The modeling team needs to run a policy on a training checkpoint that isn't a candidate, and reproducing or rerunning a policy means launching every candidate, or a few of them, at once.

`launch` and `status` now choose the models to run in one of three ways:

| Option | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `--candidate NAME`, repeatable | the named candidates |
| `--all-candidates` | every candidate (the default for `status`) |
| `--model KEY` or `--model-config FILE` | a model outside the policy, such as a training checkpoint, on every evaluation |

A model outside the policy has no overrides, and it leaves out each evaluation whose protocol window is larger than its own; the dry run and `status` list those. Its window is its `serve.max_model_len`, or else the window its checkpoint's config declares, which is then written into its config so records name it. An object-store checkpoint without an `identity`, whether supplied or a declared candidate, is identified by a digest of its files' checksums, so rewriting it in place gives its runs new IDs. A supplied model may not reuse a candidate's name with different settings. `verify` checks a run of a supplied model against the model its record names, so it needs no extra flag.

A run that succeeded but is invalid, or flagged with a ⚠ warning, is skipped like any succeeded run unless named with `--rerun RUN_ID`. That replaces its record and archive, and the success marker of any earlier job with the same runs, then runs it again. A run with no finished record can't be named, so a running job is never disturbed.

`launch` resolves every model before submitting any job, so a bad candidate, or an evaluation the policy doesn't have, fails the whole launch. A candidate excluded from the named evaluations just has nothing to run. It also leaves out evaluations whose record already succeeded, and a server with none left is never started. Before, a relaunch submitted every group, and the job found inside that its runs were cached. Run IDs depend only on the evaluation, model and policy, so the evaluations that remain keep their paths, and failed runs resume there. The dry run lists the evaluations it leaves out.

```
policy marin-2026-11-20-trial @ 68057cb3ef  candidate qwen3.5-9b
  model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B@c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a
server 1: v5litepod-4 on us-west4  max_model_len=73728  priority=batch
  aime24               limit=20  max_tokens=None  seed=42  results=gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals/pipeline-qwen3.5-9b-aime24-…/results
```

The existing Harbor agent protocols leave both unset. The worker keeps its three-pass default.

sourceStates.title: [eval] Bind sealed Micro210 to the native task runtime
sourceStates.body:
Run the sealed 434-row Micro210 protocol through native TaskSpecs and a
generation plan. Derive the 94 Pi rows from their pinned packages while
retaining row identities, repetitions, prompts, verifier resources, and
per-task provisioning. Keep the frozen Together judge and vLLM startup
settings, and verify the frozen source, converter, and image pins through the
derived table's binding receipt before launch.

Grading scope is declared per task: a `TaskSpec` declares whether its verifier
scores the workspace an agent stops at, so undeclared tasks stay unavailable
after a limit failure while the sealed Harbor protocol keeps its
stopped-workspace verdicts, and unnamed errors stay excluded from scored
denominators. A script grader declares the judge service its command needs
with a task-owned empty rubric instead of a placeholder rubric, and the judge
connection binds only to rows whose frozen grading plan consults the judge —
code-execution graders run without provider credentials. Each smoke row
selection builds its own cached conversion artifact.

BixBench's verifier uses the machine-local judge relay after Pi stops. Forward
the Together credential to CoreWeave coordinators without requiring GCP
credentials there.

A [production-priority smoke on eight RNO H100s](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fbenfeuer%2Fevaluation-micro210-native-smoke-2026.11.24.7-coordinator-b9284ed5)
from clean commit `9d0f38ca81` verified all three selected rows: BixBench 1.0,
BFCL 1.0, and CRUXEval 0.0. This proves launch, provisioning, and judge access;
full-protocol score equivalence remains unmeasured.

Focused checks pass. Broader selected checks retain 16 failures also present on
the untouched parent head, plus nine Harbor platform failures reproduced on
main. The [validation receipt](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Fmarin%2Fevaluation%2Fmicro210-native-12167%2Fevidence%2F2026.11.24%2Fvalidation.json)
records test counts, baseline comparisons, advisory responses, and retained
outcomes (`s3://marin-rno2a/marin/evaluation/micro210-native-12167/evidence/2026.11.24/validation.json`).

Review feedback from rjpower and atqamar is addressed on head `fee0efd3fc`;
the eval-ingestion definition lives in
[experiments/evaluation/README.md](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fee0efd3fc/experiments/evaluation/README.md).

Follow-up to #12167.

sourceStates.title: Alert on failed Iris controller checkpoints
sourceStates.body:
Page when the latest periodic checkpoint upload from a CoreWeave Iris controller fails. The controller reports each attempt as a numeric Finelog metric, so the alert clears after a successful upload. The runbook points to checkpoint storage credentials and explains why a refreshed Secret can leave bundle uploads failing until the controller replaces its startup S3 client.

RNO2A rejected its mounted access key with `InvalidAccessKeyId` on three checkpoint attempts before recovery ([incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1085)). Existing alerts cover controller liveness and storage capacity, but a running controller with failed checkpoint uploads had no direct alert. Node storage probes use a different bucket. The new rule requires checkpoint telemetry to reach the Marin hub; absent samples yield no checkpoint verdict.

sourceStates.title: [iris] Mask CUDA devices to the privileged task allocation
sourceStates.body:
Privileged Kubernetes GPU tasks set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` from their NVIDIA device-plugin allocation before task setup and launch. Iris resolves the assigned UUIDs or indices to PCI-ordered CUDA ordinals. This preserves numeric GPU IDs for existing launchers that parse Ray accelerator IDs as integers. Startup fails if Iris cannot match the allocation to the requested GPU count.

A privileged pod can enumerate all node GPUs even when Kubernetes reserves only a subset. Ray can then select GPUs that belong to another task. The CUDA mask guides application discovery while privileged processes retain host device access.

[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1092)

sourceStates.title: [post-training] Add SFT mixes and curriculum validation to RL
sourceStates.body:
Run a versioned SFT data mix through the existing model command, stopping at its export with --through sft or continuing into RL. Preserve the published-initializer path and pass an unbuilt SFT export as an artifact dependency. Start Mochi's mixture clock at its restored step and size its optimizer horizon and decay to the requested update budget, so a shared manifest works for either model.

Add exp7-262k-32node by porting Exp6 SFT157's native controls: MuonH, FP32 parameters/BF16 compute, special-token reseeding and update scaling, token-weighted accumulation, z-loss, CP8/DP32 expert sharding, optimizer offload and the initial C4 reference gate. Preserve its initializer and tokenizer. Apply all-position loss through a text-format consumption view with pack 256/lookahead 128; ignore cached assistant weights while excluding padding, without rewriting the release. Preserve 30 warmup updates and constant base LR, converting Exp6's wall-clock 15% cooldown to the final 15% of updates with a 0.1× floor. A frozen resolved-control fixture checks both optimizer groups.

SFT-only execution uses the preset's coordinator route, checks the materialized native configuration before submission and pins the export fingerprint across coordinator re-entry. Production priority reaches the training child. It constructs no RL selection, RL training or Micro210 stage. Exp7 requires an approved V10.1 seal and the one-epoch capacity receipt's update count. The sealed V10.1 preflight resolves 1,680 updates, 256 H100s and 262,144 positions. The initial Exp7 launch aborted in its first training-step collective before completing an update. Pin the submitted environment to Exp6 SFT157’s actual consumed configuration: CUDA backend, shared compilation cache, shard autotuning disabled and 600-second first-collective/NCCL termination limits. The legacy Grug dispatcher was outside that native launch path; remove its scheduler/slop/command-buffer overrides. Allow two failure retries per task with a 64-failure cumulative job budget. Recovery version 2026.11.26.62001 runs at production priority without rack exclusions using the earlier immutable bundle. Its attempt 0 ended at the 90-minute startup watchdog; the 30.446-second rendezvous message reported successful completion after a warning. Attempt 1 passed the training collective and reached post-step HLO uploads after finite-loss checks; full update metrics remain pending. All 32 optimized training HLOs are identical. The first-update stall mechanism remains unproven; see [incident 1088](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1088). The normalized Exp6 RL preset/curriculum remains a later binding.

For mix arms, sample 200 prompts randomly from their own admitted RL mix with a fixed seed, remove matching task/prompt identities from training and record selection provenance. Main's external family-stratified held-out panel cannot express that split; an optional typed evaluation field binds the derived train/validation selection. Evaluate and retain checkpoints every 3 updates. Select the highest arithmetic mean of the last 3 validation evaluations, requiring a full window, retaining the earlier checkpoint on ties and persisting non-winning history for restart. Keep main's 99% coverage requirement. Retain every validation checkpoint and the permanent final SFT, then export the best RL policy.

Gate arms on updates, with defaults Mochi 524 SFT / 72 RL and Snowball 360 SFT / 36 RL. The SFT exposure reference is 360 × 256 × 262144 = 24.16B positions; ceil(360 × 256 / 176) = 524 Mochi updates. At supplied Mochi 25 s/update and measured Exp4 Snowball 172.042 s/update, those imply 3.64 h and 17.20 h, excluding startup/export. Main's Mochi allocation is 704 GB200 versus 128 in that timing reference, so the timing is conditional. V5's supplied 2,100 Mochi updates imply 96.89B positions / 14.58 h, equivalent to 1,444 Snowball updates / ~69 h at the historical rate.

The [Exp4 RL reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7056588184) covers 36 × 64 = 2,304 prompt groups: 72 Mochi updates at 32×8 or 36 Snowball updates at 64×8. Supplied Mochi 14 min/update at 64×8 implies 8.4–16.8 h depending on scaling, with different GPU allocations; Snowball 12 h / 36 = 20 min/update is a budget proxy. V5/V7 inventories 142.87B/145.45B imply 3,097/3,153 batch-176 or 2,129/2,168 batch-256 token-equivalent updates, ignoring padding/weights. V5's replay-inclusive epoch is 2,988 updates; V7's 746-update audit draws 377/434 components and cycles 122. These defaults make no epoch or wall-clock guarantee.

Micro210/EvalDash waits on #12249's frozen 2026.11.23 binding. That follow-up consumes the best export and automatically publishes each sealed row through main's FineStore/EvalDash APIs, with model+checkpoint+policy naming.

Native dispatch parity checks pass: all 16 SFT launcher tests and required lint/type checks. The latest affected check passed 1,438 tests and skipped 4; four failures match independently reproduced pinned-main cases and one sandbox timeout passes in isolation. Earlier recovery checks cover both failure gates and SFT-only re-entry; advisory findings are fixed or answered.

diagnostics.title: [curation] Polaris grader rejects correct Mochi and plain-text answers
diagnostics.body:
Polaris's retained TaskSpecs request plain-text answers, but the packaged grader requires literal `</think>` followed by a boxed result. Correct plain-text answers and Mochi's `<|end_think|>` output therefore receive scored reward 0 with nonzero token-loss masks. This is a mismatch between the retained task/consumer contract and the intentionally preserved upstream format gate, not a failure of the mathematical equality check.

Two independent blinded reviews of 20 retained responses from Mochi campaign runs `.532` and `.534` agreed on 17 correct final answers and 3 missing finals. All 20 received 0. The larger retained population has 202/202 zeros; it has not been independently regraded.

Reproduce:

1. Extract the [frozen audit bundle](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-rl-data-campaign%2Fpolaris-audit%2F2026.11.26.1%2Faudit-evidence.tar.gz). Install its pinned Sympy 1.13.3, pylatexenc 2.10 and mpmath 1.3.0.
2. From the extracted directory, run:

```python
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "frozen-grader")
from grade import score
contract = json.load(open("cases/P-2-06/config.json"))
assert score("63", contract) == 0
assert score(r"\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<|start_think|>work<|end_think|>\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<think>work</think>\boxed{63}", contract) == 1
```

The same contrast reproduces for correct answers `12000` and `6` on two other tasks. Incorrect, empty and unfinished-reasoning controls return 0. This CPU repro calls the unchanged `score` function used by the CLI; local `/app` and `/tests` placement was not exercised.

Expected: the grader/binding accepts a mathematically correct answer in the task's advertised format across supported model reasoning protocols, while preserving wrong-answer and incomplete-output failures. It must not impose an undisclosed XML or boxing requirement.

Affected retained source: `open-athena/polaris-project-polaris-dataset-53k-b25e0cb8-retained-20261116-b-v1@9079512fe3d2d332b446b1b37deb9d2898f5461e`; upstream scorer revision `eda12fe22dd83aca59ec46a67147240dc483f62b`. Producer files are `experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/polaris/grade.py` and `tasks.py` on the ingestion branch. Fix forward on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` with a regression and re-seal/re-pin for future rounds. Existing campaign runs and records remain unchanged.

[Contract frozen before code inspection](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/91#issuecomment-7207765866). The bundle includes exact scripts, fixtures, dependency lock, sample selection and independent reviews. Storage: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-rl-data-campaign/polaris-audit/2026.11.26.1/audit-evidence.tar.gz`.

diagnostics.title: [eval] SWE-bench Multilingual agents can fetch upstream fixes from the internet
diagnostics.body:
SWE-bench Multilingual's curated eval (#11676) runs its agents with internet access, because the Harbor packages it lowers don't set `allow_internet`. In the 100-task panel runs, agents used it to fetch the upstream repository and read the merged fix before passing, on `sharkdp__bat-3108` and `jqlang__jq-2750`. Other runs tried package registries and GitHub without passing. Local git history is not a leak: in every attempt that listed the full history, the newest commit was the task's base commit.

The effect grows with stronger models. On SWE-bench Multilingual, [Cursor](https://cursor.com/blog/reward-hacking-coding-benchmarks) measured 9.1 points between its standard and restricted harnesses for Opus 4.8 Max, and an [NVIDIA audit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06780) found that turning off the network lowered pass@1 by 9 to 13 points for three open models, almost all of it upstream retrieval. [Inspect's SWE-bench](https://ukgovernmentbeis.github.io/inspect_evals/evals/coding/swe_bench) defaults to no internet.

The agent can't simply go offline, because each package's `test.sh` downloads its log parser with `uv` while grading, and grading runs in the agent's container. The fix runs the agent offline and grades it in Harbor's [separate verifier](https://docs.harborframework.com/news/separate-verifier-sandboxes): a fresh machine from the same image, with the network, that applies a patch of the agent's workspace taken after the agent stops. Upstream SWE-bench grades the same way, from a patch applied to a fresh container. It also keeps the agent away from the environment its tests run in.

Validation on Daytona, with the harness's hosted-model smoke loop:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Null agent (1 s), all 100 tasks | 99 graded 0 with an empty patch; every grader installed its parser over the network. 1 Daytona build failure, below |
| Hosted model, Terminus 2, 27 tasks, 15 min cap | 26 graded, 13 passed; no agent command reached the network, including on `bat-3108` and `jq-2750` (both 0) |
| `preact-2896` and `prometheus-13845`, 3 trials each | All 6 graded; patches 0.7 to 22 KB |

The smoke runs found three problems, fixed on the branch. Terminus 2 installs `tmux` at startup, so the offline images now install it at build time. One `preact` patch was killed while applying, most likely because it carried a large file such as a core dump, which Daytona sandboxes write into the working directory without a size limit; new files over 1 MiB now stay out of the patch, and a patch that fails to apply records an infrastructure error instead of a zero. `prometheus-13845`'s declarative build failed with "Image processing cancelled" on every retry in two runs, then built after a standalone build of the same Dockerfile, which suggests Daytona cached a cancelled build.

The packages now differ from the published Harbor ones in where they grade, not in what they grade. The version bump starts fresh corpora and records, so the panel needs to be rerun; Pi's option (local branch) will pick up the same setup.

diagnostics.title: [rl] Retained SWE-Gym pivot judge returns model_not_available
diagnostics.body:
The retained SWE-Gym pivot source cannot grade campaign rollouts: every one of 81 retained step-1 calls in Mochi campaign .526 returned Together HTTP404 `model_not_available` for the configured judge `glm-5.3`. The runner fails closed: score and passed are null, status is error, and every affected response has zero loss weight. This prevents the intended source from contributing to training; it is not evidence of an all-pass grader.

Reproduce:

diagnostics.title: [curation] Finish the cohort grader tamper-surface hardening per family
diagnostics.body:
The converted cohort graders (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/harbor_cohort_conversion.py`) run the verifier on the agent's machine as root and read the reward from artifacts copied off it. `7db57f9d39` hardened this: the collect sequence now kills leftover agent processes before the verifier runs and before the artifacts copy (Daytona provides no confirmed scoped descendant teardown, so an agent process that outlived its command could rewrite the reward file during the copy), and the reward path recomputes the verdict from the copied eval output, scoring zero on disagreement with the copied reward file.

The recomputation is per-family opt-in. Only the OpenSWE profile ships a verified rule (its fail-closed `OPENSWE_EXIT_CODE` marker contract over the copied eval output). The other fallback families keep the plain copy:

* swe-gym / swegym-validated: the reward derives from `/logs/verifier/native-output.txt` via an in-image adapter (`/opt/swegym-grader/bin/python /tests/native-adapter.py grade`). The adapter's own output joins `test-stdout.txt`, so the copied stdout is not byte-identical to the derivation input; the rule needs the derivation input copied separately or the re-run semantics verified.
* r2egym-patched: the derivation input `/logs/test_output.log` is not among the copied artifacts at all; `test_state.py` grades from it on the task machine.

Residual boundary, recorded deliberately: a root process racing the artifact copy on the same machine defeats any file-based integrity check, and the kill sweep is best effort (a process naming itself `daytona`, `toolbox` or `shellbox` survives by cmdline identity). The `SharedIntegrityContract`'s UID separation (agent 10001 / grader 10002) remains the stronger isolation for new SHARED SWE packages.

Done when:

* Each fallback family's recomputation rule lands with a divergence regression test (a planted reward that disagrees scores zero), or the family records why no rule is derivable from copied bytes.
* The r2egym derivation input joins the copied artifacts so its rule becomes derivable.
* The kill sweep's service-exclusion list stays validated against the live Daytona sandbox layout (planted writer dies; agent/toolbox and file round-trips survive).

1. **DSpark (PR #12239) on a Mochi Exp4 RL round (`.131`).** The round is blocked. - `.131` passes the unchanged gate, or is formally closed with the cause recorded.

issue.title: [rl] Turn-deadline expiry discards partial generations as zero-token rollouts
issue.body:
Mochi .129 archives can report `generated_tokens=0` when a turn deadline cancels a long active decode before a complete non-streaming ModelTurn reaches the recorder. This does not establish that the inference engine generated no tokens. The original blanket engine-queue-starvation diagnosis was unsupported.

The balanced 500-rollout sample contains 58 such timeout rows (11.6%). In the learner's separate consumed-batch cohort, 363/12,800 rows were verifier-unavailable (2.84%); they were token-loss masked and excluded from RLOO baselines, not trained as reward-zero failures.

Retained timing events match 29 of the 58 sampled session IDs and cover 32 request IDs with 115–19,735 generated tokens. Internal queue wait was at most 18.529 s and first-token delay at most 19.773 s. Last observed decode spans reach 1,743.155 s (median 1,291.646 s), mostly from progress events rather than completed requests. These aggregates include three sessions outside a coarse timing check. Session reuse, Ray log suppression and unobserved pre-engine waits prevent a strict causal fraction for all 58 rows. No retained event demonstrates an engine admission wait approaching 1,800 s; the overall queue-starvation share remains unknown.

The same run's step-24 Micro210 evaluation originally scored 365/434 trials. The existing BixBench regrade brings that to 375/434; the user authorized recovery of only the remaining 58 no-response slots and one verifier timeout, keeping all 375 graded outcomes unchanged.

Private sample: `open-athena/mochi-rl-129-rollout-sample`, `rollouts.parquet`, e.g. `transcripts/0125.md`. Run record: marin-community/marin-logbooks#88. Evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-zero-token-timeouts/2026.11.26.1/deadline-correction-evidence.json`.

Expected: retain the exact partial generation when an active decode reaches its deadline and run the real verifier under #10197. A genuinely never-scheduled request must use a distinct bounded admission allowance. Output length and slow decode under load need separate attribution.

Done when:

- Active deadline expiry returns exact sampled tokens, behavior logprobs, routes and policy-step stamps for verification, without a synthetic EOS or a fabricated completed response. Apply the contract to canonical evaluation as well as future authored Mochi RL recipes.
- Preserve the user's slot-ownership-clock requirement: execution budgets start/resume at actual engine scheduling, with a saturated-slot regression. This is a guard against real admission wait, not an established explanation of the sampled cohort.
- Report queue wait separately from generation time, and attribute slow decode with per-request/per-engine evidence rather than inferring it from a zero-token archive.
- Confirm unavailable rows are excluded from token loss and RLOO baselines. This masking check is complete.

Partial-retention implementation 0602a5bbdc is landed and enabled by future Mochi RL recipes; admission-clock implementation e6aeaa1813/1802d95806 is landed through 77f3e5f57a. Already submitted jobs remain pinned. Shared task-client partial return is now landed in 36098e90e2, covering future canonical evaluation without a protocol override. The already submitted exact-59 recovery remains on 77f3. GPU runtime certification and slow-decode attribution remain open.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

On [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), the total-turn timer starts when the first model request is sent, and the model-turn timer also covers engine queue time. vLLM already records QUEUED and SCHEDULED events with per-request queue wait, but that signal stays in engine logs; the model client returns only after generation. The outer attempt timer starts before harness execution, while the zero-token unavailable row appears to have both loss and baseline eligibility disabled; the latter still needs an end-to-end assertion.

**Relevant code**
- [`recorder.py#L222-L236`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L222-L236) — total-turn deadline starts on send
- [`recorder.py#L358-L369`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L358-L369) — model-turn deadline includes queue time
- [`engine.py#L162-L168`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L162-L168) — attempt deadline starts before harness
- [`request_timing.py#L35-L85`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/request_timing.py#L35-L85) — scheduler events and queue-wait evidence
- [`task_projections.py#L199-L223`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6f431fe52c3f14b03f616d6f38330eb2403447e3/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L199-L223) — unavailable-row training disposition

# Proposed Fix

This spans the rollout engine, SkyRL inference transport, Harbor trial limits, and trainer evidence, so it belongs on #11120 or a coordinated follow-up after that branch lands. #11120 is open and currently conflicts with `main`; a separate implementation PR would duplicate its branch-only rollout engine.

1. Carry a request-ID-correlated SCHEDULED notification from the vLLM engine to the pending model call. Start total-turn and model-turn budgets on first engine scheduling, including long prefill and decode. Bound pre-scheduling wait with a separate queue-admission deadline, and preserve a separate setup watchdog. Align the outer attempt and Harbor trial clocks with that lifecycle so neither can cancel a queued first request.
2. Reuse the existing per-request QUEUED/SCHEDULED/first-token timing to emit queue wait and generation durations as separate rollout metrics. Propagate them into SkyRL's train/eval telemetry; include cancelled and never-scheduled requests in queue diagnostics.
3. Add a saturated-engine regression: hold all slots beyond the turn timeout, queue a short request, confirm it remains pending, then release a slot and confirm its deadline begins. Cover a request that never gets scheduled under the queue deadline. Add a trainer test for a zero-token unavailable row that checks zero loss mask, baseline exclusion, and zero advantage with the configured estimator; document the observed disposition.

Validate with the affected CPU tests and a bounded mixed-source replay, comparing its zero-token timeout count and score coverage against the issue's 58/500 train and 69/434 Micro210 baselines.

🤖 Correction from the follow-up investigation. The diagnosis in the issue body (deadline before engine-slot ownership, queue starvation) is contradicted by the engine data.

- **Masked, not trained as zero:** all 58 sampled zero-token rows were masked and excluded from the RLOO baseline. In `.129`'s 25 consumed batches, 363 of 12,800 trajectories were verifier-unavailable (2.84%), and 395 were masked overall.
- **The engines did generate:** for the 29 affected sessions with engine timing, they generated 115 to 19,735 tokens. Queue wait was at most 18.5 s and time to first token at most 19.8 s. Across all 80 engine snapshots, the most requests running at once were 19 (`.129`) and 18 (`.131`), against a limit of 64. "Turn deadline expired before the first response" means no *completed* non-streaming response. The outer 1800 s deadline discarded unfinished generations.
- **Rates in the uniform 10% retained archives:** `.129` 212/1,786 = 11.87%; `.131` 194/2,083 = 9.31%. All of them are masked.

issue.title: [experiment] Reduce Mochi SFT doom loops with online FTPO
issue.body:
## TL;DR

Measure exact repetitive tails in Mochi SFT step 400407, then test whether online FTPO can halve per-domain incidence while retaining native task correctness. Baseline measurement precedes training.

## Description

Adapt the [Dr. Doom campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691) to Mochi. Preserve the exact tail-loop detector and FTPO objective. Use TP1/BF16 serving and Mochi's MuonH/R3 training path. The fixed, hashed evaluation panel covers math, instruction following, coding, reasoning_gym, structured outputs, and STEM MCQ. All graders are programmatic and fail closed.

## Hypothesis or Goal

For each target domain, obtain a post-training loop upper bound no greater than half its confirmed baseline count on identical prompts. Extend low-incidence 32K cohorts from 128 to 256; fewer than 10 confirmed loops after extension makes a domain non-target. Non-target upper bounds may increase by at most three. Per-domain correctness may lose at most max(3, 5% of N) passes; pooled correctness may lose at most 2% of the panel.

## Status

Native-rendered cohort v2 is published and verified (manifest SHA-256 `1c2f2b83a3b895b518e7745d3a1fe05af857f56273449c6a3aad9087f9354af3`). Corrected S0 was submitted November 24 at 19:45:04 EST, runtime `2026.11.24.4`, source `1661a15e9f`, for 128 GB200 on cw-us-east-08a at production priority. Coordinator and GPU child are running. No valid incidence count is available yet; training remains pending.

The first S0 attempt was cancelled at 19:25 EST because preparation omitted the native answer-format instruction when hashing prompts. Its outputs and v1 hash table are excluded. V2 exactly matches the saved native prompt; all 512 original math tasks remain eligible.

Seal the full baseline and sparse-domain reserves before S1. The executor clock remains November 24 17:46 EST through November 26 17:46 EST; start no training after November 26 13:46 EST.

## Links

- Prior campaign: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9691
- Source branch: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo
- Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/codex/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/logbooks/77-mochi-doom-ftpo/notebook.md

## Decision Log

- Freeze baseline prompts and detector before choosing target domains.
- Keep circular but nonperiodic reasoning out of the exact-loop objective; report length stops and open reasoning spans separately.

## Conclusion

Pending measurement.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 64 | 2 | 2 | 7 | 1 | 10 |

All192 retained training records were matched against their retention-ledger IDs and replayed through the unchanged native tail detector. There were3 exact loops and41 length caps, of which38 had no exact suffix loop. Every capped response left thinking open. The zero-target batch therefore had no exact detected cycle; candidate filtering did not lose a detected loop in these three batches. The working hypothesis is sparse exact-loop signal in uniform64-prompt math batches at16K, while much length-capped reasoning is outside this objective. This does not establish the cause of every correctness regression and does not justify widening the detector.

`chosen_win` was0 on both active batches, but it is measured before the optimizer update on fresh greedy rollouts. Under exact serving/training agreement, the rejected generated token is the argmax, so alternatives cannot already beat it. Zero is not independent evidence of no learning; the paired pilot is the relevant outcome.

The best-checkpoint record retained **global step0: the original SFT export**. No trained model was promoted, and no new HF conversion was needed. Its full-panel result is exactly the sealedS0 audit, reused by identical model identity: the50% target is unmet in every target cohort. S1 had also regressed on its separate32K smoke pilot (13loops/80passes→18loops/72passes outof128).

Run: `/benfeuer/users-benfeuer-checkpoints-mochi-doom-ftpo-doom-math-1a818f5cdd-in-728208ba-2026.11.25.3-coordinator-0fc0c701`, GPU child `ae1aa30c1c31`, source `3f18f0b54c`, qualified data2026.11.25.2, runtime2026.11.25.3. issue.title: [long-loop] Ablate the RL optimizer and learning rate for Mochi and Snowball
issue.body:
Mochi and Snowball long-loop RL need an ablated optimizer and learning rate. Since the 2026-11-23 normalization, both models use MuonH with `lr` 1e-5 and `adam_lr` 2.307692307692308e-6 (`offload_momentum: true`), `max_grad_norm` 0.5 and 64 prompts × 8 samples per batch. Snowball moved from AdamW to MuonH for memory: AdamW state did not fit at long context without CPU optimizer offload, and offload slowed each step. Neither the optimizer nor the learning rate came from an ablation. The earlier tuned Snowball RL comparison in #7786 (hypothesis V) found that AdamW learned faster and reached a higher peak training reward than MuonH. This experiment should settle both choices for each model. It is planned here and not yet scheduled.

Design:
- Curriculum: our best RL curriculum at the time it runs, identical for both models. Record its identity and version.
- Fixed settings: the normalized config for all other settings (staleness 3, 98,304-token response cap and 131,072-token context, batch 64 × 8, `max_grad_norm` 0.5), one seed per arm, and the frozen 200-row validation split from the curriculum.
- Optimizer arms: (a) MuonH with `offload_momentum: true` and the `adam_lr`/`lr` ratio held fixed; (b) AdamW with CPU optimizer offload. Each arm uses the qualified trainer layout for its memory profile.
- Grid per optimizer and model: half-decade steps. MuonH starts at 3e-6, 1e-5, 3e-5 and 1e-4. AdamW starts at 3e-7, 1e-6, 3e-6 and 1e-5. Learning rates do not transfer between optimizers.
- Metric: an EMA of validation accuracy over the first 20 optimizer updates (EMA window 5, matching best-checkpoint selection). Report raw per-eval accuracy and training reward alongside it.
- Cost: report median seconds per update and GPU-hours per update for each arm, split into rollout wait, optimizer step and offload transfer. AdamW with offload wins only if its accuracy gain justifies its step-time cost.
- Adaptive grid: if the best arm of an optimizer is at either edge of its grid, add the next half-decade step beyond that edge and repeat until the best value is interior.
- Stability checks per arm: training/inference mismatch KL, gradient norm and the clipped-gradient fraction. Report any divergence as a result, not a rerun.

Done when:
- Each optimizer has a learning-rate curve per model whose best value is interior to its grid, with EMA validation accuracy at 20 updates and seconds per update per arm.
- A recommended optimizer and learning rate per model is stated, with the accuracy, cost and stability metrics that support it.
- The long-loop RL defaults are updated, or confirmed unchanged, from that recommendation.

comments.body:
🤖 This requires at least eight 20-update GPU arms across Mochi and Snowball. The long-loop runtime is in [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), currently open with merge conflicts; curriculum versioning is in [#11659](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11659). The current [Mochi round](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b6cb1427505405e651ea2e7b5e91b102c1e7956e/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-three-rack.yaml#L27-L31) still specifies 32 prompts per batch, and its [optimizer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b6cb1427505405e651ea2e7b5e91b102c1e7956e/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-three-rack.yaml#L71-L83) uses `1e-5` with `max_grad_norm: 0.0`; the sweep needs new, pinned arm specs.

Plan:
1. Pin one tested runtime revision, both pre-RL checkpoints, the chosen curriculum identity/version, training-pool hashes, and its disjoint 200-row validation split. Resolve #11120's merge conflicts or record the exact tested branch revision. Post these pins and the validation-accuracy scoring and missing-score rules here before launching.
2. Build eight fresh RL run versions: Mochi and Snowball at `3e-7`, `1e-6`, `3e-6`, and `1e-5`. Hold the curriculum, seed, 20-update limit, batch of 64 prompts × 8 samples, gradient clip `0.5`, staleness 3, 98,304-token response cap, and 131,072-token context fixed. Validate each rendered plan and diff each model's arms so learning rate is the only within-model change.
3. Evaluate the same 200 rows at updates 2, 4, …, 20. Preserve per-row scores and scored counts, apply the existing 180/200 selection coverage gate, and report raw accuracy at each evaluation and the five-evaluation EMA at update 20. Record training reward, training/inference mismatch KL, gradient norm, clipped-gradient fraction, and any divergent arm without silently rerunning it.
4. If either model's best rate is at a grid edge, run its next half-decade rate and repeat until the best is interior. Compare accuracy and stability, publish the curves and links to runs and pinned configs here, then recommend one rate per model. Update or confirm the long-loop defaults in a PR linked with `Fixes #12103` after the recommendation.

🤖 Update: Snowball long-loop RL is moving from AdamW to MuonH, the optimizer Mochi already uses, so both models now share one optimizer. The ablation therefore sweeps the MuonH learning rate for both models. The starting grid moves to MuonH scale, centred on Mochi's current 1e-5: 3e-6, 1e-5, 3e-5, 1e-4, widened past any edge winner as described above. AdamW learning rates from earlier Snowball runs do not carry over.

🤖
# Research

The round-one entry records pinned SFT/RL sources and configs, an immutable checkpoint revision, Micro eval policy and scores (439/440 attempts scored), and archive receipts. [PR #11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120) contains the open long-loop implementation and reports the RL admission failure. Issue #11337 has no later measured recipe or specific code defect to address.

**Relevant code**
- [`run_spec.py#L71-L113`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/run_spec.py#L71-L113) — resolves and validates pinned configs.
- [`audit_results.py#L15-L92`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/eval_runtime/audit_results.py#L15-L92) — audits scored and unscored attempts.
- [`archive.py#L72-L98`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12fefdef4a1e10a17b1ee33d54de49efb2e2271f/experiments/post_training/long_loop/archive.py#L72-L98) — seals and verifies evidence.

# Proposed Fix

Keep this issue open as the measured-recipe index. For each new run: (1) pin the SFT/RL source commits, complete run specs, exact data files and mixture weights, then validate the pins; (2) publish the selected immutable checkpoint revision, Micro eval policy, scored/unscored counts, both aggregate means, benchmark scores, and provenance/archive receipts with explicit gaps; (3) add the recipe as a comment and update the summary table. Assign a new recipe version whenever code, data, sampling, or grading changes.

🤖 The recipe ledger is [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337). Its first entry records the completed round-1 model, pinned SFT/RL configs and data mixes, the Micro policy and all 20 benchmark scores, the public HF revision, and the private provenance archive.

Under the user's subsequent explicit cleanup request, removed 12 superseded native checkpoints: SFT steps 1, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 and 700; abandoned run `2026.11.11.2` RL steps 1–2; and run `2026.11.12.5` RL steps 12 and 14. This removed 173,721 current objects totaling 6,439,134,545,120 bytes (6.44 TB; physical billing reduction was not measured). All 12 prefixes verify empty. Retained SFT step 746 (`2026.11.09.12`) and selected RL step 16 (`2026.11.12.5`) match their pre-cleanup object sets, sizes and ETags. Base weights, HF exports, data, logs and the evidence archive remain. Fifty-two metadata backups were read back and hash-verified before deleting the checkpoints. Receipt: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop/evidence/20261113-intermediate-checkpoint-cleanup/completed.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Flong-loop%2Fevidence%2F20261113-intermediate-checkpoint-cleanup%2Fcompleted.json)).

This is a manual cleanup record. The original archive's incomplete-evidence flags remain unchanged; it does not certify W&B provider completeness or erase the unscored DNA assembly attempt UID399.

🤖

### Long-loop round 2, November 2026

SFT completed 204 optimizer updates, numbered 0–203, and retained native checkpoint 203. RL completed 20 updates and selected checkpoint 20 by eligible validation-reward EMA. Export, final evaluation, public HF upload and the private evidence archive completed with limitations. The original coordinator failed at its report coverage gate after successful RL, export and evaluation; CPU post-processing completed without replaying training or policy sampling. The completion receipt is dated November 15, 2026, 10:49:53.982839 UTC (05:49:53.982839 EST).

Model: [open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round2-2026.11.14.13 at `6546ba2d5a1d44992d6376d4c51c1a69f16b1d10`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-LongLoop-Round2-2026.11.14.13/tree/6546ba2d5a1d44992d6376d4c51c1a69f16b1d10), OpenMDW-1.1. The completion receipt records 49 verified files / 39 weight shards matching the producer export.

#### Configs and launch

No round-2 downloadable recipe tarball or dedicated recipe-bundle manifest was found in the long-loop evidence prefix or round-2 archive inventory. The round-1 tarball describes a different recipe. The uncertainty calculation follows the prior Exp3 seal and [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197). Each benchmark uses the conservative task-level SEM bound `s = 0.5/sqrt(10*0.9)`, including the 90% valid-trial allowance. With scored fractions `r_b`, means `m_b` and weights `w_b=1/20`, set `mu=sum(w_b*r_b*m_b)`, `delta=sum(w_b*(1-r_b))` and `sigma=sqrt(sum((w_b*r_b*s)^2))`. The Imbens–Manski critical value solves `Phi(c+delta/sigma)-Phi(-c)=0.95`; here `c=1.9381`. The interval is `[mu-c*sigma, mu+c*sigma+delta]`, clipped to [0,1]; benchmark intervals use one cell. Identified bounds assign missing rewards values in [0,1] without sampling uncertainty, so they are not confidence intervals. Repetitions are not independent tasks; these intervals do not measure serving-stack reproducibility.

### Coverage, errors and audit

All 440 frozen attempt IDs occur exactly once. Reporting retains 418 scoreable attempts across 18 cells; this includes the ten verifier-completed but uninformative TruthfulQA attempts. Removing TruthfulQA leaves 408/430 scoreable attempts (94.88%) across 19 informative declared benchmarks, of which 17 have scores. The remaining 22 trials are absent; no missing reward is imputed.

- **BixBench: 0/10.** Nine verifier `ValueError` exceptions state: `Provider credentials must remain on the host; use a Shellbox model relay: OPENAI_API_KEY` ([#12094](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12094)). One sandbox creation returned `DaytonaError:502 Bad Gateway`. None has a verifier grade.
- **Terminal-Bench 2: 28/30 (93.33%).** Two `VerifierTimeoutError` trials on `mcmc-sampling-stan` reached the frozen 300 s verifier limit. Both are absent.
- **CRUXEval: N/A.** All ten zero-score traces were reviewed through the frozen input program, model assertion, parsing and retained verifier diagnostics. Nine output literals are correct; five of those also use the requested answer tags. All ten verifier processes exited 0 and printed 0.0. The zero does not pass the trace audit. The frozen cell is rejected under [#11922](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11922), as in the SFT baseline. No semantic replacement scores are assigned. These receipts do not establish the exact subprocess mechanism for each zero.
- **TruthfulQA: uninformative.** All ten prepared rows put a true answer at option A ([#12060](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12060)). Its observed value enters no capability mean. In fixed-panel bounds only, the cell is unknown in [0, 1].

The ten Harbor `AgentTimeoutError` trials retain six verifier zeros and four verifier ones. The 24 `ContextLengthExceededError` trials retain 19 zeros and five ones, under #10197’s Harbor rule. All other unnamed or infrastructure-classified failures remain absent. Native rows and policy bytes are unchanged.

Approximate intervals use the [existing `evalrecords` Imbens–Manski bounded-missing-panel implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c751a4907dc7d2053c85b13c7ce57dab9c7737bf/lib/evalrecords/src/evalrecords/eval_stats.py), with an independent-task normal approximation. Each benchmark uses a conservative task-level standard-error bound `0.5/sqrt(10*0.9)`, which includes the policy’s 10% infrastructure-failure tolerance. Repeated trials are not independent tasks. Unknown cells and absent trials are bounded in [0, 1]. The informative attempt-weighted 95% interval is **29.27%–57.82%**. With ten tasks per benchmark, these are descriptive approximations, not exact finite-sample coverage guarantees. They exclude serving-stack reproducibility.

🤖 **BixBench re-scored offline on every sealed 2026.11.23 Micro210 row** — coverage repair for the pass@1 table (#10197)

**Cause.** Every `bixbench-pi` trial in these rows ended `"Harbor trial has no verifier score"`: the Harbor trial-config rebuild round-tripped the verifier env through a redacting serializer, which turned the judge-relay placeholder `OPENAI_API_KEY="EMPTY"` into the literal `"****"`, and Harbor's task-environment boundary rejected that literal before the verifier ran (`ValueError: Provider credentials must remain on the host; use a Shellbox model relay: OPENAI_API_KEY`). So the one judge-required Harbor row produced `n_scored 0` everywhere and silently dropped out of pass@1. Fixed by 4fd392c07a (`[skyrl] Keep the projected verifier credentials through the Harbor trial rebuild`); a fresh bixbench-only run on the fix scores 3/10 with real judge verdicts.

**Method (no GPU re-runs).** The archived per-trial trajectories are complete, so each trial's proposed answer was extracted with the package's own `<answer>` rule and graded offline with the frozen judge binding (`micro210_inputs.bixbench_judge_resources`: Together `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, strict `binary_score` schema, max_tokens 1024, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, reasoning_effort low — the same client the prepared tasks run in-container). 52 answered trials judged, 0 judge failures; trials with no answer in the trajectory failed closed to 0 (#10197: agent failures score 0, only genuine infra errors are excluded). 🤖
# Research

The converted TaskSpec exposes the original problem as its only user message, with no answer-format instruction. Its packaged scorer instead concatenates the problem and response, requires literal `</think>`, and calls a vendored extractor that returns no answer without `\boxed`; the math comparison is never reached for correct plain text or Mochi output. The producer lives in draft Atlas PR #11277, while long-loop PR #11120 carries the frozen retained-source pin but not the producer files.

**Relevant code**
- [Polaris conversion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/57abfb47f2ff2c3da172a94c805fd828d4684593/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/polaris/tasks.py#L37-L53) — public task and packaged grader
- [Polaris scorer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/57abfb47f2ff2c3da172a94c805fd828d4684593/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/polaris/grade.py#L12-L26) — format gate before math check
- [Packaged test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/57abfb47f2ff2c3da172a94c805fd828d4684593/experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_polaris.py#L25-L55) — current format expectations
- [Long-loop pin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dfd38c88b43c5f2e114d1d85ad48b8f849eb2d7a/experiments/post_training/long_loop/campaign/source_pins.json#L2800-L2823) — retained release consumed by campaign

# Proposed Fix

1. Change the Atlas producer's `grade.py` to score the response alone. Extract a completed final answer after either supported reasoning closer, or use the whole response when it contains no reasoning span. Accept a boxed or unambiguous plain-text final, reject empty and unfinished reasoning, and keep the pinned math comparison helpers unchanged. Update the rubric and vendored-adapter documentation to describe the TaskSpec contract rather than the upstream format gate.
2. Replace the existing packaged-grader format expectations with a regression covering the audit's correct plain text, boxed, XML-think, and Mochi outputs for `63`, `12000`, and `6`; keep wrong-answer, empty, unfinished-reasoning, and prompt-delimiter controls at zero. Run the packaged test with its declared parser dependencies.
3. Bump the Polaris converter version and seal a new immutable retained release. Re-run the new pin's census, deduplication, lexical and SAMPLE qualification gates; compare the 20 independently reviewed responses against the new grader and inspect the other 182 before making any claim about recovered accuracy.
4. Update the Atlas retained pin and the long-loop `source_pins.json` to the new release revision through their existing PRs, then validate the consumer binding. Preserve the original release pin and historical campaign records. The producer, release and consumer changes span two active integration branches, so a one-file PR would leave future rounds on the broken pin.

🤖 The script runtime supplies the final assistant message through PlainText.extract; the legacy Polaris test simulates a full XML reasoning trace, which the real consumer does not deliver. I will add a versioned, exact-input-guarded retained-task adapter on long-loop that replaces only the grader entry script and ships the existing shared last-box/last-line extractor. The original task IDs, public questions, references, machine requirements and mathematical checker bytes stay unchanged. A real retained-task regression will show plain 63 failing before and passing after, while incorrect and empty submissions remain zero.

Publication remains gated: a disposable last-box/last-line replay recovers 12 of the 17 reviewed positives; five require additional extraction/normalization work. The shared math grader also needs care for categorical references (for example, a symbolic interpretation can confuse a word with a reordered spelling). I will not re-pin or release the held mixes on the strength of a partial format fix. Existing runs remain unchanged; the corrected release, full fixture qualification and loop-push landing will be reported separately.
