12392.body: Working on this in loom: https://loom.oa.dev/s/ipwn9hw8

🤖 Holistic review of e8e099929603a01b01524f3756a07f46234d4a3a.

The PR fixes a real loss. When a turn deadline fires during a non-streaming vLLM decode, the sampled tokens are now kept and graded instead of the row being archived as a zero-token unavailable turn. Since the last review, the change has narrowed to one deadline path and the recorder decides the stop reason. I have no open findings.

**System**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  worker["TaskRolloutWorker"]:::changed -->|"InferenceClock.scope()"| recorder["_Recorder deadlines"]:::changed
  recorder -->|"model call"| client["InferenceEngineClient"]:::changed
  client --> ray["RayWrappedInferenceEngine._scheduled_call"]:::changed
  ray -->|"*_with_scheduling stream"| vllm["AsyncVLLMInferenceEngine"]:::changed
  vllm --> timings["RequestTimings"]:::added
  ray -->|"abort_active_partial_request"| vllm
  clock["rigging.inference_clock"]:::added -.-> recorder
  clock -.-> ray
  clock -.-> relay["ModelRelay / AgentInferenceBackend"]:::changed
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Before.** The recorder armed the total-turn budget at the first request and wrapped each model call in `asyncio.timeout(model_turn_timeout)`. When either expired, the Ray call was cancelled and the turn had no response, so the row was archived as unavailable. Time spent waiting in the engine queue counted against those budgets.

**Design.** `TaskRolloutWorker` binds a ContextVar `InferenceClock` to each attempt. The recorder still arms its model-turn and total-turn budgets at the first request. When the vLLM actor streams a `RequestScheduled` notice, `clock.scheduled()` rebases them so they start at scheduling. Queue waits pause the budgets and are bounded separately by a cumulative `inference_queue_timeout` (2280 s). After scheduling, `RayWrappedInferenceEngine._scheduled_call` waits until shortly before the nearest execution deadline, with a margin of up to 30 s. If tokens exist, it asks the engine to abort, awaits the original collector, and marks the turn `partial_deadline`. `_Recorder._partial_deadline_reason` maps that marker to `model_turn_timeout`, `total_turn_timeout` or `attempt_timeout`, whichever of its own active budgets is nearest. It then grades the turn and stops the trial. The vLLM actor contributes only the scheduling stream, the request-timing log and `abort_active_partial_request`. Harbor is unchanged.

**Evidence and limits.** These ran locally at this head:
- The admission and transport-deadline tests in `test_inference_admission.py` and `test_rollout.py`: 9 passed.
- `test_request_deadline.py`, `test_task_deadline_transport.py` and `test_request_timing.py` under the SkyRL `cpu` extra: 10 passed.
- A probe with a clock in scope and a transport that never reports scheduling. It now stops at the 0.3 s turn deadline with `total_turn_timeout`, the same as without the clock.

As the body says, nothing has exercised GPU vLLM. Two claims still rest on reading the pinned vLLM: that `AsyncLLM.abort` emits the accumulated tokens, logprobs and routes as a final output, and that serving_chat returns an aborted output as a normal response. The new stop reasons `model_turn_timeout` and `attempt_timeout` have no consumer in the repository that enumerates stop reasons.

No findings.

Earlier findings, all resolved:
- 1: The recorder arms its budgets at the first request again, and scheduling only rebases them. A new test covers a transport with no scheduling notice.
- 2: The transport emits a neutral `partial_deadline`, the recorder chooses the reason, and the `rolloutengine` imports are gone from `inference_engines`.
- 3: The engine-local `request_timeout_seconds` path and the `scheduled` parameter are deleted.
- 4: The Harbor edits and the README claim about Harbor are reverted, and `wait_execution` is removed.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:e8e099929603a01b01524f3756a07f46234d4a3a -->

🤖 Removed stale README and docstring wording and an incidental error-message assertion. The author had already removed Harbor's unused clock wiring. Four focused SkyRL tests pass; Pyrefly reports missing dependencies across this worktree.

<!-- marin-deslop:44ad7dd218511963eeeb4b2420960720cf2c6067 -->

🤖 Addressed the four findings in e8e0999296 and 490bbc0266. Recorder deadlines now arm at the first request and rebase on scheduling; a clock-scoped transport without a scheduling notice still times out. The Ray transport returns a neutral partial-deadline marker, and the recorder labels it using the same nearest clock timer that triggered the abort. I removed the unused engine-local timeout and Harbor clock edits. Added regressions for the no-notice fallback and model-turn versus total-turn attribution; the focused suites and Marin lint pass. GPU abort behavior still needs runtime certification.

🤖 Holistic review of a29942f82f238d764221bba32b919794cd225d83.

This change keeps the tokens a model already generated when a turn deadline fires during an active decode. Before, a canonical Micro210 trial whose non-streaming request was still decoding at the deadline was archived as a zero-token unavailable row; the report counts 78 of 434. After this change, the request carries engine scheduling notices back over the Ray stream. A per-trial `InferenceClock` (new, `rigging/inference_clock.py`) pauses execution budgets while a request waits for an engine slot. Shortly before the nearest execution deadline, the transport calls `llm.abort` and returns the partial output, which the recorder grades and attributes to the governing budget (`model_turn_timeout`, `total_turn_timeout` or `attempt_timeout`).

The mechanism is coherent, and the CPU coverage of the clock, the deadline helper and the transport is good. My concerns are about reach: the clock is installed for **every** vLLM-backed SkyRL task attempt, so RL training changes behaviour too, not just canonical evaluation. The PR body doesn't describe that. The core GPU path is also unverified.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix (consequence):** `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py:554` wraps every `backend == "vllm"` attempt in an `InferenceClock`, training rollouts included. `InferenceEngineClient._wait_for_generation_to_resume` (`inference_engine_client.py:1132`) then charges weight-sync pause time to the cumulative 2,280 s queue allowance. A long agentic training trial that crosses several weight syncs can now fail with `InferenceAdmissionTimeout` and become a no-response trajectory, where it previously just waited. With multi-minute syncs and long steps (for example Mochi at about 25 min per step), that budget is reachable. Separately, `execution_timeout` re-arms the attempt deadline to the full `attempt_timeout` at first scheduling (`inference_clock.py` `_resume`), so `attempt_timeout` no longer bounds attempt wall time in training. Either scope the clock to evaluation, or exclude weight-sync pauses from the admission allowance, and state the training-side behaviour in the PR body.
- **2. Should fix (consequence):** `vllm_engine.py:119` and `:1301` flip `disable_log_stats` to `False` for every AsyncVLLM engine. The removed comment says this flag only suppressed vLLM's duplicate console stat logger, because the custom interval logger already keeps stats on. Presumably the flip is there because scheduler `QUEUED`/`SCHEDULED` request events are recorded only when `log_stats` is on. If so, keep it, but suppress the duplicate console logger (for example by passing only the custom `stat_loggers`) and mention the engine-wide change in the body, since it affects training engines' logs and per-step overhead.
- **3. Should fix (evidence):** the central claim, that `abort_active_partial_request` makes the pinned vLLM abort path emit the accumulated tokens, logprobs and routes as a final output (`vllm_engine.py:1414-1420`), is exercised only through CPU fakes; the body says GPU behaviour is unverified. Canonical Micro210 scoring will depend on this path. Before merge, run one real-engine check: a single request with a short `model_turn_timeout` that is decoding when the deadline fires. Verify that the returned token count equals the engine's generated count and that logprobs and policy steps are aligned.
- **4. Should fix (consequence):** `ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py:379` raises `ValueError("Trial admission requires one inference request")` for any multi-prompt `generate` while a clock is active. Because finding 1 installs the clock on every vLLM training attempt, any in-trial batched generate path (group or best-of-n sampling within one trial) would now fail. If no such caller exists today, add an assertion-level test documenting the single-request contract. Otherwise, support per-request admission.
- **5. Should fix (fit):** `remote_execution_watchdog` (`inference_clock.py`) returns `2 * seconds + queue_remaining`. The factor of 2 is an unexplained magic number in a safety watchdog. Name it as a constant with the reason (relay round-trip slack), or derive it from the budgets it protects.
- **6. Related PR:** #11850 (one retry policy) merged into `main` and touches the same `engine.py`, `recorder.py`, `models.py` and `task_worker.py`; this branch is now DIRTY. #12249 (Micro210 native binding) also edits `engine.py` and `task_worker.py`. Rebase onto current `main`. Since #12249 is the consumer of canonical Micro210 behaviour, landing this one first and then rebasing #12249 avoids a double conflict.

**Evidence and limits.** I read the full diff against merge base `fa29ec5c63`, including the new `inference_clock`, `request_deadline`, `request_timing`, the vLLM and Ray transport changes, the recorder attribution and the shellbox relay timeout plumbing. I didn't run the GPU path. The CPU suites cited in the body were not re-run here.

issue.title: [rl] Mochi 50-step RL data-mix campaign
issue.body:
## TL;DR

A week-long ablation over RL data mixtures on Mochi. Each candidate mix of 4–8 Atlas sources at equal weight trains for 50 RL steps with the RL config of run `.131` held fixed. Each run's best checkpoint by validation reward is then evaluated on Micro210. Three runs go at a time. Results are being collected.

## Description

The RL config is fixed at that of `long-loop-mochi-exp4-dspark-rl-2026.11.25.131`: DSpark, 128 GB200 = 48 trainer + 80 rollout, TP1/BF16, the .131 initializer. Only the curriculum changes, to an equal-weight mix (1/k per source). Each run is 50 optimizer steps with no wall-clock budget. A run stops early only when it is clearly broken, for example a data defect, all-zero rewards or a grader error storm.

Every mix has at least 2 SWE/agentic families and at least 2 competition-math families. Every source has at least 500 tasks. Sources Mochi had already saturated at the start of RL are left out (nemotron_if, openscience). The candidates come from the holiday Atlas burndown (marin #12329): v2 has 50 mixes and v3 has 50 more.

The queue follows human priority ratings: High, then Medium, then Low. Mixes with a source whose stored grader predates fixes on main run after all clean mixes, until those sources are re-sealed. Mixes run as listed, including sources that are Pending in the served R40 catalog, at their declared pins. Each run records which of its sources diverge from the catalog.

## Run table

Ground truth for every campaign run. Update it with `~/.local/bin/campaign-runs set`.

<!-- campaign-runs:begin -->

issue.title: [experiment] Measure Mochi action loops and loop guards
issue.body:
## TL;DR

No tested guard met the complete registered loop-reduction rule. **S1-stop came closest:** it missed only TBLite's 50% bar, achieving **42.5%**, and correctness passes under the user's **×0.75 override**.

## Status

**Closed as completed on November 26, 2026, under the final user disposition.** All measured runs, audits and required conservation are complete. No registered repeat remains. **I4 is UNPERFORMED** because its required pinned 216-store manifest is unavailable; **no follow-up run**. No exports, new compute or deletions; conserved artifacts remain unchanged.

## Conclusion

S1-stop, repetition penalty and antithrash RL after four updates each fail their registered loop gates. Correctness passes the user-reduced thresholds. **I3 remains FAIL + UNDERPOWERED:** treatment logged zero antithrash fire fraction and mean penalty at every update, so this pair does not establish the efficacy or causal harm of actively applied antithrash. The experiment is closed with these negative results and limitations.

[Final notebook and user disposition](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b84d32f6f7e5c587f4c3ed4a14e1efbcef52fc5e/logbooks/86-mochi-loop-guards/notebook.md). [Index PR #87](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/pull/87) is ready for review; validation passes and the coordinator will merge it.

## Recorded protocol and results

Can Mochi action loops be cut by at least 50% while holding correctness? S0 is sealed. Both inference guards and fixed-N4 antithrash RL fail their registered loop gates. Under the November 26 **user override** lowering correctness thresholds by 25%, both guards pass correctness. The RP repeat no longer has a registered trigger and was canceled; its root and GPU child are verified killed.

The **user override** extending every recorded clock by 24 hours restores antithrash I3. T0 remains November 25 12:01:36 EST; T20 is November 27 08:01:36, T32 November 27 20:01:36, and the deadline November 28 12:01:36 EST. N=4 updates is fixed for both S2 arms before submission, based on the existing conservative seven-hour update budget plus three hours for startup. The initial revision3 pair failed before training on the NVML output-pointer defect. Revision4 is accepted from pushed source `ecc9fb1bae`, which also uses main's valid Ray fabric-label encoding. Control accepted November26 13:51:23.963 EST and treatment13:51:46.099 EST. Both passed physical placement.
